title: Tier-aware SLA probation, progressive fallback optimizer, and simulated circuit-breaker tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional surges and backend slowdowns we see noisy 429 spikes and elevated p99 latencies that trigger blunt fallbacks and full-tier degradations. Current circuit-breaker thresholds are static and per-route, causing oscillation for tenants near the margin and suboptimal model-variant choices (e.g., switching to a lower-quality quantized model when a short-lived cache cold-start is the real cause).

Goal: Implement a tier-aware probation window and progressive fallback optimizer that: 1) uses a composite trip score (error rate, p95/p99 latency, 429 spike pattern, and recent QPS) with EWMA smoothing, 2) assigns per-tenant and per-tier probation intervals to avoid immediate hard-cutovers, 3) chooses fallback model variants probabilistically to allow quality-preserving canaries, and 4) exposes a simulator to tune hysteresis and circuit-breaker gains before rollout.

Why this is important: reduces customer-visible quality regressions, prevents cascade failovers across tiers/regions, and gives SREs a reproducible way to tune fallback aggressiveness without production hammering.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New trip scoring metric emits for every route with fields: trip_score (0-1), contributor breakdown (5xx_rate, 429_rate, p95, qps), and probation_state (open/probation/closed)
A2: Probation window logic prevents hard fallback for a tenant if probation_state=probation and trip_score < probation_cutoff for the entire interval — validated with synthetic spike tests

A3: Progressive fallback chooses fallback variants in increasing cost/quality order with probability ramping (e.g., 10% -> 30% -> 100%) before full switch; labeled experiments show <5% regressions in response-quality metrics for 95% of tenants in staging
A4: Simulator produces recommended hysteresis parameters (decay_alpha, probation_seconds, spike_detection_window) and an offline calibration CSV for runtime-1.25 rollout
A5: Dashboard: per-route and per-tenant visualization of trip_score, probation windows, and recent fallback decisions in Console release runtime-1.25
A6: No customer-facing SEV incidents attributable to premature fallbacks in 2 weeks post-rollout for canary tenants (monitoring checklist in rollout_plan)
A7: Unit and integration tests cover trip scoring math, state transitions, and probabilistic sampling for fallback selection
design_notes: Trip score is a weighted sum of normalized signals: normalized_5xx, normalized_429_spike_score (based on sudden derivative of 429 rate), normalized_p99_latency, and squared-normalized_qps_penalty. We use EWMA on each signal with configurable alpha per-signal.

Probation: when trip_score crosses the open threshold, we set tenant->tier into 'probation' for probation_seconds. During probation we only execute progressive fallbacks (partial sampling) and collect quality telemetry. Only if trip_score remains above hard_threshold for probation_seconds do we flip circuit to open for the tier.

Progressive fallback: maintain ordered model variant list (e.g., base_fp16 -> quantized_int8 -> smaller_model) and a ramp schedule keyed by time_in_probation and evidence. Sampling uses reservoir sampling with deterministic hashing by request id for reproducibility.

Simulator: a traffic replay engine that can inject synthetic 429/timeouts/error patterns and run a grid sweep over parameters (alpha, probation_seconds, ramp steps). Produces false-positive/negative curves and expected customer-quality loss estimates.

Regional considerations: trip scoring incorporates region-specific signal baselines; a regional aggregate modifier biases decisions to prefer cross-region slowdown fallback only when local recovery unlikely (based on cross-region variant capacity and recent error-correlation)

Safety: add kill-switch flags: global, region, and tenant-level opt-out. Default conservative settings for S0 tenants (free-tier) vs SLA-backed tenants (tier 1) — SLA tenants get longer probation and stricter thresholds to avoid accidental degradations.
implementation_steps: 1) Add trip_score generator into router service: compute per-request signals, EWMA update, and emit metrics (1 week) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/router/PR/9876
2) Implement probation state machine persisted to routing metadata store (etcd) with TTL semantics and admin inspection APIs (2 weeks)
3) Progressive fallback engine in decision layer: sampling scheduler, deterministic hashing, and variant catalog hooks (2 weeks)
4) Build simulator: traffic-replay tool in go/python that consumes historical traces and synthetic injectors; CI job to run parameter sweeps (1.5 weeks)
5) Extend Console: new trip_score panels, per-tenant probation timeline, and rollback controls (1 week)
6) End-to-end integration, staging canary (select 3 low-risk tenants), and gradual ramp to 20% of traffic before full rollout (2 weeks)
7) Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window with automated alerting thresholds and rollback playbook
telemetry_metrics: fallback_decision events with chosen_variant, sampling_probability, and reason_code
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dev team only — run simulator and short-lived staging canary
Stage 1: Staging canary with synthetic traffic and 3 internal test tenants (monitor for regressions)
Stage 2: Production canary — 1% of production routes, pick tenants with robust SLOs and low churn
Stage 3: Ramp to 20% over 72 hours if metrics stable, otherwise rollback to previous routing policy
Stage 4: Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics for the canary cohort
Rollback criteria: sustained >10% increase in user-level failure-rate, >5% increase in perceived quality loss metric, or manual SEV from SRE/Support
testing_plan: Unit tests: trip_score math, EWMA behavior, probation transition boundaries
Integration tests: end-to-end path with fallback sampling and deterministic hashing
Simulator tests: replay historical incidents and validate that recommended parameters avoid over-triggering
Chaos tests: inject region-level delays and 429 floods in staging to validate hysteresis and cross-region bias
User studies: for canary tenants, measure nlg-quality delta on sampled requests when fallback variants used
